svg.title: CH-R2 with ADS1115

text.tspan: CH-R2 2-wire resistance meter, PCB version: sensed by the ADS1115 · schematic (PROPOSED)
R_dut = R_REF · V_node / (V_top − V_node). Same circuit as the Phase 1 perfboard, but the three voltages are read by a 16-bit ADC with one shared reference, and a self-test path is added.
SDA and SCL: 4.7 kΩ pull-ups to 3V3
(once per board, on the mainboard I²C bus)
C 100 nF + 1 µF, close to VDD
Single-ended inputs, PGA ±4.096 V (±0.512 V for the node on low ohms), 128–860 SPS.
A second ADS1115 (0x49) footprint is on the board for the 4-wire channel (Phase 4).
Footprint for the ADS1115 breakout module header (DNP) is the fallback.
• Read order per range: V_top, V_node, V_top again. Only one drive pin is high at a time, the other is INPUT.
Turn-off: drive the pin LOW for 20 ms, then INPUT.
• Self-test (clips open): close PR3, measure on the 1k range (expect 470 Ω ± 3 %); then PR4 on the 10k range
• R 1 kΩ + C 100 nF on each top-sense line: charge reservoir for the ADC input. Settling is about 100 µs.
• R_REF1 / R_REF2: 0.1 % parts. 1 % parts work if their measured values go into hw_pins.py.
⚠ Resistance of coils at rest only (≤ 3.3 V)
Never connect the DUT clips to a coil that is wired to a CDI, to a spinning pickup, or to any CDI output or
ignition coil. The TVS and clamp handle static and the turn-off kick only. A pickup that is spun produces tens of
volts: use CH-PU for that. See docs/safety.md.
